methods.name: Mixed Model for Repeated Measures
methods.label: MMRM
methods.description: Linear mixed model for longitudinal data with structured R-side covariance. No random effects (G-side); within-subject correlation modeled through the residual covariance structure.

formula.default_expression: response ~ covariate + repeated_factor + fixed_effect + repeated_factor:fixed_effect | repeated_subject / repeated_factor
formula.notes: The part after '|' specifies the repeated measures structure: subject is the clustering unit, time is the repeated factor within subject. methods.name: Baseline Observation Carried Forward
methods.label: BOCF
methods.description: Uses the baseline value as the imputed value for all missing post-baseline observations within a partition. Conservative strategy assuming return to baseline.

formula.notes: The baseline value is propagated to all rows within the partition. This is a lookup, not a carry-forward — the imputed value is the same regardless of when the observation is missing.

inputs.name: baseline_value
inputs.description: The baseline value for the subject/parameter (typically BASE or value at ABLFL='Y')

inputs.name: partition
inputs.description: Grouping variables defining scope (typically subject, parameter)

methods.name: Last Observation Carried Forward
methods.label: LOCF
methods.description: Computes the last non-missing observed value within a partition, ordered by a time variable. The result carries forward the most recent non-missing value and is intended as input to M.Imputation.

formula.default_expression: imputed_value := LOCF(value) OVER (partition ORDER BY time_order)
formula.notes: LOCF scans backwards in time_order within each partition and returns the most recent non-missing value. If no prior non-missing value exists, the result is missing.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Source value to carry forward (may contain missing values)

inputs.name: partition
inputs.description: Grouping variables defining the carry-forward scope (typically subject, parameter)

inputs.name: time_order
inputs.description: Variable defining the temporal ordering within partition (e.g., AVISITN, ADY)

methods.label: Mean Imp
methods.description: Computes the arithmetic mean of all non-missing observed values within a group as the imputed value. Common for baseline covariates or when a group-level central tendency is an appropriate replacement.

formula.notes: The partition defines the scope of the mean computation. For subject-level mean imputation, partition by subject. For group-level, partition by treatment group. The mean excludes the missing values being imputed.

inputs.name: value

inputs.name: group_partition

methods.description: Computes the median of all non-missing observed values within a group as the imputed value. More robust to outliers than mean imputation.

inputs.name: value

inputs.description: Grouping variables defining the median computation scope

methods.name: Worst Observation Carried Forward
methods.label: WOCF
methods.description: Uses the worst (most extreme) observed value within a partition as the imputed value. Worst is defined by the direction configuration: 'high' takes the maximum, 'low' takes the minimum.

formula.notes: WORST is an alias for MAX when direction='high' (e.g., adverse events, lab toxicity) or MIN when direction='low' (e.g., efficacy scores where lower is worse). Only non-missing observed values up to the current time are considered.

configurations.name: direction
configurations.description: Which direction is 'worst': 'high' = MAX is worst (e.g., toxicity), 'low' = MIN is worst (e.g., efficacy where higher is better)

configurations.name: scope
configurations.description: Whether to consider only values observed up to the current time point (cumulative) or all observed values in the partition (all_observed)

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Source values from which the worst is selected

methods.name: Zero Imputation
methods.label: Zero Imp
methods.description: Uses a fixed constant (default 0) as the imputed value for all missing observations. Simplest strategy; appropriate when missingness can be interpreted as absence of the measured quantity (e.g., zero cost, zero count).

configurations.name: constant

methods.name: Unit Conversion
methods.label: Unit Conv
methods.description: Convert a numeric value from its per-row source unit to a fixed target unit, using a scalar factor looked up in the unit_conversions vocabulary keyed by (source_unit, target_unit). Linear conversions only — non-linear conversions (e.g. temperature) require a different method.

formula.default_expression: result := round(value.value * factor(value.unit, target_unit), precision, rounding_method) [target_unit]
formula.notes: Algorithm reads the input Quantity's .value (decimal) and .unit (code) fields, applies the scalar factor from the unit_conversions vocabulary, and produces a Quantity with the target unit. Single Quantity output combines the converted value and target unit.

configurations.name: target_unit
configurations.description: Target unit code. Valid values are resolved at runtime from the distinct to_code / to_name entries in unit_conversions.json, filtered by the physical dimension of the source measure. No default — must be chosen per transformation.

configurations.name: precision
configurations.description: Number of decimal places to round result to after multiplication. If null/unset, no rounding is applied. For complex rounding rules, leave null and chain M.Rounding downstream.

configurations.name: rounding_method
configurations.description: Rounding convention when precision is set. Same enum as M.Rounding. Ignored when precision is null.

configurations.name: on_missing_factor
configurations.description: Behaviour when no (source_unit, target_unit) entry is found in the vocabulary. fail: raise an error. na: set result to NA. passthrough: keep the original value unchanged.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The Quantity to convert (value + unit). Algorithm reads both .value (decimal) and .unit (code) fields. Resolves via Observation.Result facet → SDTM --ORRES + --ORRESU.

methods.name: Windowed Visit Assignment
methods.label: Windowed Visit Assignment
methods.description: Assign each observation to a scheduled analysis visit using day-windows and a target-day tie-break. SAP-style AVISIT derivation. Consumes a pre-computed study day (SDTM --DY) relative to the randomization anchor; no date subtraction inside the method.

formula.default_expression: analysisVisit := window.label WHERE day ∈ [window.dayMin, window.dayMax], tie-break closest(|day-targetDay|) then min(visitNumber)

configurations.description: Identifier of the BC that provides the randomization anchor (e.g. BiomedicalConcept_216 'Subject is Randomized'). Documents the SAP's day-zero; not consumed at runtime because --DY is already relative to this anchor.

configurations.description: Scheduled visit windows: array of { label, visitNumber, dayMin, dayMax, targetDay }. dayMin/dayMax=null means unbounded.

configurations.name: tieBreak
configurations.description: Tie-break rule when multiple windows match the day.

inputs.name: day
inputs.description: Pre-computed study day (SDTM --DY column) relative to the randomization anchor. Positive = after anchor, zero/negative = at/before anchor.

inputs.name: partition
inputs.description: Subject-level partitioning. Not used by the default template (assignment is row-wise on day).
